title: chance
content_html:
chance

The dice in Catalogue change the order in which works are encountered. In 3 symbols, intuitive selections, incidental limits and a predetermined procedure helped make an image. Chance can enter at different points in making or looking. Which decisions are handed over to it, and which begin when the result appears? The I Ching and the Library’s writing on random numbers offer further ways to ask how an encounter comes to mean something. Catalogue randomness · 3 symbols

Reading note. Jung. In his foreword to the Wilhelm–Baynes I Ching, Jung describes how a cast of coins enters into the interpretation of the moment. The cast and the Catalogue shuffle both produce an encounter. How much of its significance comes from what happens to turn up, and how much from the situation of the person reading it? Jung’s foreword to the I Ching, collected works vol. 11 · Jung × I Ching in the Library
